provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Lowest-ticket category in the family: one-person businesses, so software and AI prices sit well under the build. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The trainer's specialties named plainly: post-rehab strength, seniors' balance, postpartum return, weight loss, sport-specific conditioning, and who they refer elsewhere
pageStructurePlus.why: People hire a personal trainer who has helped someone like them. A named specialty beats a generic 'all fitness levels' every time.

pageStructurePlus.section: Where the trainer coaches: in-home, park or studio
pageStructurePlus.contains: In-home sessions with the neighbourhoods covered and equipment brought, park sessions, the private studio or gym the trainer uses, and travel fees
pageStructurePlus.why: Location decides the hire before price does. Busy parents and seniors book the in-home trainer who clearly comes to their part of town.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How remote coaching works: the programme app, weekly check-ins, form video reviews, messaging hours, and who online coaching suits better than sessions
pageStructurePlus.why: Online coaching lets a trainer sell past their local hours. Buyers need to see exactly what they get each week before they pay monthly.

pageStructurePlus.section: Health questionnaire before the first session
pageStructurePlus.contains: A PAR-Q style health and injury questionnaire, when the trainer asks for a doctor's clearance, and how past injuries shape the first programme
pageStructurePlus.why: Older and injured clients worry a trainer will hurt them. A careful intake shows the trainer takes their body seriously.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Training with a spouse or friend, small groups of up to four, how the split price works, and how sessions adapt for different fitness levels
pageStructurePlus.why: Partner sessions make a personal trainer affordable for more people, and couples who train together stay longer.

designDirections.name: Book a Session
designDirections.bestFor: Solo trainers and online coaches who need one page with a consult button and a clear specialty
designDirections.headlineSample: Personal training in {City} that fits your schedule
designDirections.whyItFits: Magenta Signal suits a creator-style coach with a social following, and the grotesque sans keeps one strong headline and one booking button.

designDirections.name: Friendly Coach
designDirections.bestFor: Trainers who work with beginners, seniors and postpartum clients and sell session packs
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Sky Kite's soft rounded type feels unintimidating to nervous beginners, and the card stack shows specialties and packs side by side.

designDirections.name: Private Client
designDirections.bestFor: High-end in-home trainers serving executives and private clients at top rates
designDirections.whyItFits: Private Vault's quiet palette and refined serif read like a concierge service, and a type-led hero suits clients who value discretion over gym shots.

openers.line: Your Google listing as a personal trainer has a phone number and nothing else, so someone searching an in home personal trainer in {City} can't see who you help or how to book.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the personal trainer page behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your bio link points back to the same Instagram profile, so a follower ready to hire a personal trainer has nowhere to book or see packages.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note where it lands: nothing, a link page, a form. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Your fitness coaching packages and booking, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The trainer site on your listing still shows a gym you may no longer train at. A new client checking out a personal trainer notices old details first.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old gym, old prices, a dead form. Note it.

openers.line: I opened your personal trainer site on my phone and the packages ran off the screen. People look up fitness coaches on their phone after a bad week.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same trainer, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: To start with you as a personal trainer, someone has to DM and wait. A consult booking would grab the person who finally decided tonight, before they change their mind.
openers.hook: Look for any booking or consult form. If it's DM or call only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A free consult booking for your personal training: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your client progress posts are the best thing on your trainer page, and they're buried under workout clips. A page of client stories would keep selling your coaching.
openers.hook: Find a recent client milestone post: a first push-up, a race, a strength gain. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Your fitness coaching results, where a new client decides: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say you were patient with someone who hadn't exercised in years. Those words should sit right beside the personal trainer booking button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about patience, injury or confidence. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Personal trainer reviews beside the consult booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is when people start counting weeks to a wedding or a beach trip and look for a fitness coach. The trainers with a clear package and booking get the call.
openers.hook: Use this from January to April, or in September for holiday events. Name the moment.
openers.linkLine: A twelve-week personal training package page: {demo-link}

openers.line: People decide to hire a personal trainer late at night after a rough day. Right now that decision has to wait for you to answer a DM in the morning.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking 'how do I start' or 'do you have openings'. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A trainer page that books the consult at 11pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're bringing on another personal trainer. Clients will want to see both coaches' specialties before choosing a slot.
openers.hook: Only if they posted about hiring, a new coach or a growing team. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A personal training page with both coaches: {demo-link}

openers.line: You train clients at home, but nowhere says whether you come out to {Neighborhood}. People hiring an in-home trainer check that before anything else.
openers.hook: Only if they mention in-home or mobile training. Check whether areas are listed.
openers.linkLine: An in-home personal training page with your areas: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a session or package price for your personal training anywhere. People comparing trainers often pick the one with a number on the page.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for session or package pricing. If none, the angle holds.

openers.line: Your personal trainer certifications and specialties are why someone with a bad knee should trust you, and they don't appear anywhere a new client looks.
openers.hook: Look for certifications in their bio or posts. Never invent one.
openers.linkLine: Your trainer credentials next to your coaching: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your personal training clients mostly come from other clients. When a few move away, their replacements will look you up first.
openers.hook: Look for reviews saying 'my friend recommended' or posts about a full schedule. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred fitness client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a great result for your client. A coaching win like that should be the first thing a new personal training client sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest client win post and name it exactly, with the client's permission in mind.
openers.linkLine: That client win, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a great client result.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and only found your social pages, with no packages or a way to book a consult. I put together a sample personal trainer page with your specialties, where you train and a consult booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got buried under client texts. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It shows who you train, where you train, your packages, a health questionnaire and a consult booking. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for personal trainers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss between sessions. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with your specialties, where you train and a consult booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and package changes. For a solo trainer I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes between your morning clients?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.handler: "Then the page is for raising your rate and keeping a waitlist. When a client moves away, the next one is already waiting instead of you starting from zero."

objections.objection: My clients all come from Instagram.
objections.handler: "Instagram builds trust. The site is where a follower books the consult and fills in the health questions without a DM back and forth. It links straight to your profile."

objections.objection: The gym I train at handles my clients.
objections.handler: "That works until you leave or raise your price. A site in your own name keeps your clients with you, wherever you train."

objections.objection: I can't afford a website right now.
objections.handler: "Fair. It's sized for a solo trainer, and a deposit plus monthly instalments keeps it to roughly one package a month while it's being paid."

objections.objection: I'm moving to online coaching anyway.
objections.handler: "Even better. Online clients can't meet you in a gym, so the site is the whole first impression. The online coaching page is already in the demo."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's specialties, packages and a consult booking. One new client on a package covers most of it."

email.subject: Trainer site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for personal trainers in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a consult booking. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} trainer demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — January is when people finally book a personal trainer, and they book the one they can find at night. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one client's package for a couple of months. Solo trainers think in sessions, so the build has to be small.
Offer a deposit and monthly instalments. Cash flow, not value, is what stops a trainer saying yes.
Only add the online coaching page for trainers who already coach someone remotely.
Price the in-home area page by the number of neighbourhoods, not by page.
Keep monthly add-ons under the price of one session. Anything more gets cancelled the first slow week.
Sell in October and November for January, and in March for wedding and summer goals.

lineItems.description: Max with injury questions, a clearance prompt for older clients and goal fields sent to the trainer before the consult.
Max with weekly check-in explained, a sample programme week and a monthly sign-up.
Max when it lists every neighbourhood covered, travel fees and the equipment the trainer brings.
Max with a client story, a typical first month and the trainer's training for that specialty.
Max with partner pricing, auto-renewing monthly packages and a cancellation policy acknowledgement.
Max when the questionnaire, packages and consult booking are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Trainer headshots and session action shots
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An hour shooting you coaching a willing client, plus a proper headshot, so your personal trainer page looks like the person they'll meet."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booked with a client who agrees in writing to appear.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile for a solo trainer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A Google profile set up properly as a personal trainer with service areas, then a short post each week, so local searches find you instead of the big gym."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, or at build if they have no profile at all.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after a client's first month
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Four weeks into training, when they feel the difference, clients get a text asking for a review of their personal trainer."

whatElseYouSell.name: New Year fitness coaching ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Small, tightly targeted local ads for your consult booking from late December to February, aimed at your specialty, paused when your calendar fills."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November. Ad spend is on top and kept small.

whatElseYouSell.name: Referral card and client gift kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Cards your clients hand to friends with a free consult code, so the referrals you already get arrive straight at your booking page."

whatElseYouSell.name: Short-form workout video editing
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You film a few exercise clips each week on your phone, and they come back as captioned short videos for your fitness coaching page."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they already post but hate editing.

withoutAI.route: Physical therapists who hand off finished rehab clients
withoutAI.whoPays: The clinic, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The physical therapist who sends you clients after rehab needs a page aimed at people ready for training. Your referral link goes both ways."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The handoff from therapy to personal training is a real referral path, and both sides benefit from making it visible.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each dietitian, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The dietitian you send personal training clients to for meal plans needs a booking page. Your recommendation is the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trainers and dietitians swap clients constantly, and dietitians in private practice often have no site.

withoutAI.route: The private training studio the trainer rents
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The studio where you rent hourly space needs a page that lists every trainer and rents open hours. You can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Studio owners need renters and clients for them. A tenant trainer is the natural introduction.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each therapist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The massage therapist your training clients see after hard weeks needs online booking. I'll build it with your page linked."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same clients, same goals, and a trainer's word carries weight.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The senior centre where you run balance classes has no activity calendar online. I'll build one families can see."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trainers who teach there are trusted by the staff, and centres market to adult children.

withoutAI.route: Wedding dress boutiques and bridal stylists
withoutAI.whoPays: Each boutique, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The bridal boutique that sends brides to your pre-wedding training needs a booking page for fittings. Your introduction opens the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pre-wedding training is a real referral loop, and boutiques book on fixed timelines.

withAI.route: Discharge-to-training handoff assistant for physical therapists
withAI.pitchLine: "When a patient finishes rehab, the clinic's assistant explains next-step training options and books a consult with a trusted trainer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clinics want discharged patients to keep progressing. It never gives medical advice, only next steps.

withAI.route: Meal plan question assistant for dietitians
withAI.pitchLine: "Fitness clients ask 'can I swap this meal' at night and get an answer from the dietitian's own plan rules, with anything medical sent back to the dietitian."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dietitians answer the same swap questions all week. Saving those evenings is easy to value.

withAI.route: Hourly rental booking assistant for the studio owner
withAI.pitchLine: "Independent trainers ask about open hours and rates, and the assistant books studio time and collects payment."
withAI.whyItWorks: Unbooked hours are lost rent. Each booking has a price.

withAI.pitchLine: "A client mentions a tight back after training and gets offered the therapist's next open slot, with a rebook nudge later."
withAI.whyItWorks: Solo therapists can't answer mid-session. A small fee beats one missed booking.

withAI.route: Activity question line for senior centres
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents and their adult children ask which balance and strength classes with the visiting trainer run this week and whether they're gentle enough, and get answers from the centre's calendar."
withAI.whyItWorks: Front desks at senior centres answer the same questions all day, often to worried families.

withAI.pitchLine: "Brides on a pre-wedding fitness plan ask about appointment times and alterations deadlines, and the boutique's assistant books fittings backward from the wedding date."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fittings run on deadlines, and missed enquiries go to the next boutique.

softwareAI.name: Session reminders and late-cancel rule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients get a reminder the evening before each personal training session, and a late cancel is charged automatically under your stated rule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30, or the first time a client no-shows. Needs their cancellation rule and calendar access.

softwareAI.name: Package and session-count tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each client's remaining sessions shown to them and to you, with a renewal prompt when two are left, so nobody trains free by accident."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs current client packages, even from a notebook.

softwareAI.name: Client workout log and programme sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every client's programme, weights and notes in one place you open on your phone mid-session, instead of a dozen notes apps."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their current programming format.

softwareAI.name: Consult enquiry responder for trainers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'Do you work with bad knees' and 'what do you charge' get answered from your own page while you're coaching, with the consult booking link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs specialties, packages and areas. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Package renewal nudge
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a client's personal training package is nearly used, they get a friendly renewal message with their progress since starting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, once the package tracker is live.

softwareAI.name: Online coaching check-in form
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Online coaching clients submit weight, sleep, steps and a form video each week in one tidy check-in you review on Sunday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for trainers with remote clients. Needs their check-in questions.

softwareAI.name: Check-in summary writer for online coaching
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each online client's weekly check-in becomes a short summary with what changed, so the fitness coach replies in minutes instead of an hour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once check-ins are flowing. Coach approves every reply. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Partner session split billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Partner and small-group training sessions split the price between clients automatically, so the trainer never chases a friend's half."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, if they train partners or small groups. Needs the split rules.

softwareAI.name: Trainer review thank-you drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a client reviews their personal trainer, a short personal thank-you is drafted in your voice for you to send from the car."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review asks. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Exercise clip captioner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a squat or deadlift clip, and a caption with the coaching cue and who it helps is ready in your fitness coach voice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Travel-time aware booking for in-home training
softwareAI.pitchLine: "In-home personal training slots only open when there's time to drive between clients, so a booking never strands you across town."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for mobile trainers. Needs areas and typical drive times.

softwareAI.name: Missed-week check-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A client who skipped a week of personal training gets a no-guilt message from you and a link to rebook, before skipping becomes quitting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs session history.

softwareAI.name: Programme draft helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From a new client's questionnaire and goals, a first-month training programme is drafted in your exercise library for the personal trainer to edit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their exercise library and programming rules. Trainer approves every programme. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Intake red-flag summary
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The health questionnaire comes back as a short note highlighting injuries and anything needing a doctor's clearance, before the first session."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, with the consult booking live. Never gives medical advice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Progress photo and measurement vault
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients' progress pictures and measurements stored privately with their consent, shown side by side at renewal time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a consent wording the client signs.

softwareAI.name: Small-group class booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Boot camp or small-group personal training sessions sell as spots with a cap, so one hour of coaching pays several times over."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, if they want to add groups. Needs times, caps and price.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed client comeback
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients who stopped training get a note before January with a restart offer from their old personal trainer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past client list.

softwareAI.name: Habit coach texts between sessions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Between sessions, clients get short check-ins on steps, water and sleep in the trainer's voice, and anything worrying goes to the trainer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the trainer's habit rules and client opt-in. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Exercise video library for clients
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients look up how the trainer cues each exercise in their programme, so homework sessions look like coached ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the trainer to film short exercise demos.

softwareAI.name: Client fit screener for online coaching
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Online coaching applicants answer a few questions and the coach sees a short fit summary first, so calls only go to people the coach can help."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once online coaching has a waitlist. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the trainer site as a low monthly subscription
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One personal trainer template with consult booking, packages and the session tracker, set up in a day for a small monthly fee. Volume beats custom here."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: There are many trainers and each one has a small budget. A subscription turns a skip category into a volume one.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The certifying organisation, per graduating trainer or annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every new certified personal trainer needs a site on day one. Bundle a starter page with your certification and they launch as businesses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Certifiers sell careers. A launch kit is a reason to choose their course, and every graduate is a future upgrade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Private training studio owners renting to many trainers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your studio rents to a dozen independent trainers. A trainer directory with each one's booking page fills your hours and keeps them renting."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract covers many trainers, and studio owners profit when their renters are busy.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fitness equipment retailers' trainer referral network
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Customers buying a home gym want someone to show them how to use it. A find-a-trainer page with local in-home trainers sells more equipment."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers want buyers to use what they bought, and in-home trainers are the answer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency resale of the trainer template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency gets personal trainer enquiries it can't price low enough. License my template and set them up in an afternoon."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies turn these small jobs away. A cheap, finished template makes them worth taking.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your staff could book personal training sessions with vetted local coaches on a page you subsidise. I'll build the sign-up and booking."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Employers want wellness they can count, and the trainer client is the first coach on the list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your residents want balance and strength sessions with a trainer they trust. A booking page for visiting trainers makes it a marketed amenity."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Communities sell activities to families, and trainers who already work there make the introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your building gym sits empty. A resident booking page for a weekly visiting personal trainer turns it into an amenity you can advertise."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Property managers compete on amenities, and the trainer client supplies the coaching.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Online coaching creators with a following
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each coach, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Online fitness coaches with an audience need an application page and check-in system, the same one I built for a local trainer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Online coaches aren't bound to a city, so the market is wider and the build is already done.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each specialist, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Trainers who specialise in pregnancy and postpartum fitness need the health questionnaire and gentle tone this site already has."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Specialists search for tools that fit their niche, and the intake is the hard part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "With a handful of personal trainers in {City} on the template, I approach coaches in neighbouring towns with real examples to show."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Trainers rarely compete across towns, and live examples make the low-price pitch credible.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue an abandoned coaching app setup
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You paid for a coaching app and never finished setting up the programmes or payments. I can finish it in a week, having done it for another trainer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck trainers are already paying monthly for something unused, so finishing it is an easy yes.

upsellLadder.offer: Trainer site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The personal trainer site and the care plan go on one contract, with instalments, so a package change is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a client no-show or a late cancel they didn't charge.
upsellLadder.line: "That late cancel cost you a session. Reminders and a stated rule stop most of them."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after a client's first month
upsellLadder.trigger: The first clients booked through the site reach four weeks of training.
upsellLadder.line: "Your newest clients feel the difference now. That's the week to ask for a personal trainer review."

upsellLadder.trigger: They admit losing count of a client's remaining sessions.
upsellLadder.line: "No more guessing who has sessions left. Clients see it, you see it, renewal prompts itself."

upsellLadder.trigger: They say they miss consult enquiries while coaching back-to-back sessions.
upsellLadder.line: "While you're coaching, the responder answers 'do you work with bad knees' and books the consult."

upsellLadder.offer: Online coaching check-in form and summary writer
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a client moving away who wants to keep training remotely.
upsellLadder.line: "That client moving away can stay on as online coaching, with weekly check-ins you review in minutes."

upsellLadder.trigger: It's November and their January calendar has open slots.
upsellLadder.line: "Your January has room. Small local ads to your specialty fill it before the rush passes."
